# What This Script Does

The paper shows the federal election and Saxony side by side in one figure.
The single-election figures are saved in `data/processed/figures/` (scripts 22, 23, 32, 33);
this script uses patchwork to put them together and writes the combined figures to `output/figures/`.

patchwork alone is not enough, for three reasons:

1. **Headers.** Each plot gets a header with its election ("Germany", "Saxony").
   The header should span the plot's text (from the y-axis title to the legend or last tick label),
   but patchwork only knows where the panels are.
   So the text around each panel is measured (*Measuring a Plot*) and the header's margins are set from it (*Headers*).
2. **Fixed spacing.** Headers and the gaps between rows should be the same height in every figure, in cm,
   while the plots share the rest of the height. This grid is built in *Combining*.
3. **Size.** The figure is as wide as the text (16 cm) and as high as its subfigures plus headers and gaps,
   so the subfigures keep their proportions.

# Settings

```{r settings}
label_federal <- "Germany"
label_saxony  <- "Saxony"

header_fill   <- "grey88" # shade of the header above each plot
header_size   <- 17       # pt on the canvas, printed at 8.5 pt like the axis titles (figure_scale = 2)
header_height <- 0.45     # printed cm
header_space  <- 0.15     # printed cm between a header and its plot
row_gap       <- 0.35     # printed cm between two rows of plots
column_gap    <- 0.04     # space between two columns of plots, relative to the width of one plot panel
figure_width  <- 16       # printed cm, the text width
```

# Figures

One row per combined figure.
`panels`: the subfigures, federal first, then Saxony.
`layout`: rows x columns, filled row by row:

- `1x2`: federal left, Saxony right
- `2x2`: federal row on top, Saxon row below
- `2x1`: federal on top, Saxony below


# Building Blocks

## Measuring a Plot

The header above a plot "Germany" or "Saxony" should span the plot's text, not just its panel.
patchwork only knows where the panels are, so the text around each panel is measured here.
`ggplotGrob()` turns a plot into a table ("gtable") of columns, e.g.
`| margin | y-axis title | y-axis labels | PANEL | legend | margin |`;
the panel column stretches, all others have a fixed width.
All widths are in pt on the canvas (twice the printed size, `figure_scale = 2`).

The four functions build on each other:

**`width_pt(grob)`** converts the width of one drawn element ("grob") to pt. Used by all the others.

**`part_width(g, part)`** returns the width of one named cell of the table `g`.

- Input: `g = ggplotGrob(p)` and the cell's name, e.g. `"xlab-b"` (x-axis title), `"ylab-l"` (y-axis title), `"guide-box-bottom"` (legend below the panel).
- Returns 0 if the plot has no such cell.
- Axis titles stretch with the panel, so their cell reports width 0; the function measures the title's text instead.
  An empty title (`""`) has no text and counts 0.

**`last_tick(p)`** describes the last tick label of the x-axis, which can stick out past the right edge of the panel.

- Input: the ggplot `p` (not the table), because the tick positions come from `ggplot_build()`.
- Returns a one-row tibble: `tick_pos`, the tick's position on the panel (0 = left edge, 1 = right edge),
  and `tick_half`, half the width of its label (the label is centred on the tick).
- The label is redrawn with the font size and family of the plot's `axis.text.x.bottom` theme element to measure it.
- Without ticks it returns `tick_pos = 1, tick_half = 0`.

**`measure_plot(p)`** combines these into one row of a tibble per plot:

| column | what it measures |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | all columns left / right of the panel, margins included |
| `content_left` | the text left of the panel: from the y-axis title (or, without one, the y-axis labels) up to the panel |
| `content_right` | everything right of the panel except the outer margin (e.g. a legend on the right) |
| `xlab`, `legend` | width of the x-axis title and of a legend below the panel; both are centred on the panel and stick out by half of what they exceed it |
| `tick_pos`, `tick_half` | from `last_tick()` |

A patchwork (the subfigures of Figure C.7 are already combined plots) has no single table, so it is not measured and gets `left = NA`.

```{r measure}
# Width of a grob in pt
width_pt <- function(grob) grid::convertWidth(grid::grobWidth(grob), "pt", valueOnly = TRUE)

# Width in pt of one part of a plot table (g = ggplotGrob(), part e.g. "xlab-b"), 0 if it is missing or empty
part_width <- function(g, part) {
  # g$layout lists the name of every cell, g$grobs holds what is drawn in it (same order)
  grob <- g$grobs[g$layout$name == part]
  if (length(grob) == 0) return(0) # the plot has no such part
  grob <- grob[[1]]
  # an axis title reports width 0: take the width of its text instead (none for an empty title "")
  if (inherits(grob, "titleGrob")) {
    texts <- keep(grob$children, ~ any(nzchar(.x$label)))
    return(max(0, map_dbl(texts, width_pt)))
  }
  width_pt(grob)
}

# Last tick label of the bottom axis: its position on the panel (0 = left, 1 = right) and half its width in pt
last_tick <- function(p) {
  # the x-axis as drawn on the (first) panel, after ggplot has computed the breaks
  x <- ggplot_build(p)$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x
  # all ticks with their labels; breaks outside the axis range are NA and dropped
  ticks <- tibble(pos = x$break_positions(), label = x$get_labels()) %>% drop_na()
  if (nrow(ticks) == 0) return(tibble(tick_pos = 1, tick_half = 0))
  last <- slice_max(ticks, pos, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) # the rightmost tick
  # the font of the tick labels: a complete theme (e.g. theme_bw()) is used as is,
  # theme() tweaks are added to the default theme first
  theme <- if (isTRUE(attr(p$theme, "complete"))) p$theme else theme_get() + p$theme
  text <- calc_element("axis.text.x.bottom", theme)
  # draw the label again in that font to measure it
  label <- grid::textGrob(last$label, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = text$size, fontfamily = text$family))
  tibble(tick_pos = last$pos, tick_half = width_pt(label) / 2)
}

# Widths of a plot around its panel, in pt (left = NA for a patchwork such as Figure C.7):
#   left, right:      everything left / right of the panel, including the plot margins
#   content_left:     the text left of the panel: y-axis title (if there is one) and y-axis labels
#   content_right:    anything right of the panel except the margin (e.g. a legend on the right)
#   xlab, legend:     x-axis title and legend below the panel, both centred on the panel
#   tick_pos, tick_half: last tick label, see last_tick()
measure_plot <- function(p) {
  if (inherits(p, "patchwork")) return(tibble(left = NA_real_))
  g <- ggplotGrob(p) # the plot as a table of columns
  w <- grid::convertWidth(g$widths, "pt", valueOnly = TRUE) # width of each column; the panel column ("null") counts 0
  column <- seq_along(w) # column numbers, to select columns left / right of the panel
  # the panel's cells (several with facets), each with its first (l) and last (r) column
  panel <- g$layout %>% filter(str_detect(name, "^panel"))
  panel_first <- min(panel$l) # first and last column of the panel
  panel_last  <- max(panel$r)
  # the text left of the panel starts with the y-axis title if it has text, else with the y-axis labels
  start <- if (part_width(g, "ylab-l") > 0) {
    g$layout %>% filter(name == "ylab-l") %>% pull(l) %>% first()
  } else {
    g$layout %>% filter(str_detect(name, "^axis-l")) %>% pull(l) %>% min()
  }
  # add up the widths of the columns on each side of the panel
  tibble(
    left          = sum(w[column < panel_first]),
    right         = sum(w[column > panel_last]),
    content_left  = sum(w[column >= start & column < panel_first]),
    content_right = sum(w[column > panel_last & column < length(w)]), # the last column is the margin
    xlab          = part_width(g, "xlab-b"),
    legend        = part_width(g, "guide-box-bottom"),
    last_tick(p)
  )
}
```

## Headers

```{r headers}
# Header with the election name: shaded box with plain text like the axis titles,
# or only the name in bold (shaded = FALSE)
# margin_left, margin_right: space in pt between the edges of the plot's column and the header
make_header <- function(label, margin_left = 0, margin_right = 0, shaded = TRUE) {
  # an empty plot from 0 to 1 in both directions, filled by the box with the label in its centre
  header <- ggplot() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0, ymax = 1, fill = if (shaded) header_fill else NA) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = label, size = header_size / .pt,
             fontface = if (shaded) "plain" else "bold") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, margin_right, 0, margin_left))
  wrap_elements(full = header) # spans the whole column, not only the panel
}

# Headers above all plots of a figure, each covering its plot's text
# patchwork aligns the panels: plots in the same column share the widths left and right of the panel
make_headers <- function(plots, labels, columns) {
  # one row per plot: its widths, election name and column in the figure
  sizes <- map(plots, measure_plot) %>%
    list_rbind() %>%
    mutate(label = labels, column = columns)

  # Figure C.7: its parts have boxes of their own, so only the name in bold
  if (anyNA(sizes$left)) return(map(labels, make_header, shaded = FALSE))

  # after aligning, the space left / right of the panel in a column is that of its widest plot
  sizes <- sizes %>%
    group_by(column) %>%
    mutate(column_left = max(left), column_right = max(right)) %>%
    ungroup()

  # Width of one panel in pt: the canvas without the widths around the panels and the gaps between the columns
  # canvas = n_columns * panel + (n_columns - 1) * column_gap * panel + around, solved for panel
  canvas    <- figure_width * figure_scale / 2.54 * 72 # printed cm -> pt on the canvas
  around    <- sizes %>% distinct(column, column_left, column_right) %>% summarize(sum(column_left + column_right)) %>% pull()
  n_columns <- n_distinct(columns)
  panel     <- (canvas - around) / (n_columns + (n_columns - 1) * column_gap)

  sizes %>%
    mutate(
      # how far the text sticks out right of the panel, the largest of:
      #   content_right: a legend or other text right of the panel
      #   x-axis title / legend below: half of what they are wider than the panel
      #   last tick label: half its width minus the distance from its tick to the panel's right edge
      overhang = pmax(0, content_right, (xlab - panel) / 2, (legend - panel) / 2, tick_half - (1 - tick_pos) * panel),
      # header margins: from the column's edge to where the text starts / ends
      margin_left  = column_left - content_left,
      margin_right = pmax(0, column_right - overhang)
    ) %>%
    select(label, margin_left, margin_right) %>%
    pmap(make_header) # one header per plot, in the order of the plots
}
```

## Combining

Each row of plots takes four rows of the grid: header, space, plots, gap (no gap after the last row).
Columns of plots are separated by a narrow gap column.
Headers, spaces and gaps have fixed heights, the rows of plots share the rest in proportion to the subfigures' heights.

```{r combine_functions}
cm    <- function(x) grid::unit(x * figure_scale, "cm") # fixed height, printed cm on the 2x canvas
share <- function(x) grid::unit(x, "null")              # share of the remaining height

# Combined figure of the saved subfigures (panels): plot and printed height in cm
combine_figure <- function(layout, panels) {
  n_columns <- as.integer(str_sub(layout, 3, 3)) # "2x2" -> 2

  # One row per subfigure: the saved plot, its height, election name and place in the figure
  # (filled row by row: with 2 columns, subfigures 1, 2 form row 1 and 3, 4 row 2)
  cells <- tibble(panel = panels) %>%
    mutate(
      saved  = map(file.path("data", "processed", "figures", paste0(panel, ".rds")), readRDS),
      plot   = map(saved, "plot"),
      height = map_dbl(saved, ~ .x$width * .x$aspect), # printed height of the subfigure in cm
      label  = if_else(str_ends(panel, "_federal"), label_federal, label_saxony),
      row    = (row_number() - 1) %/% n_columns + 1,
      column = (row_number() - 1) %% n_columns + 1
    ) %>%
    group_by(row) %>%
    mutate(row_height = max(height)) %>% # a row is as high as its highest subfigure
    ungroup()

  # text widths for the headers are measured with the device of the PDF
  grDevices::cairo_pdf(tempfile())
  headers <- make_headers(cells$plot, cells$label, cells$column)
  grDevices::dev.off()

  # Position in the grid: headers and plots of row r in grid rows 4r - 3 and 4r - 1, column c in grid column 2c - 1
  grid_row    <- 4 * (cells$row - 1)
  grid_column <- 2 * cells$column - 1
  design <- c(area(t = grid_row + 1, l = grid_column),  # headers
              area(t = grid_row + 3, l = grid_column))  # plots

  # Heights of the grid rows: header, space, plots, gap for each row of plots
  row_heights <- cells %>% distinct(row, row_height) %>% pull(row_height)
  heights <- map(row_heights, ~ grid::unit.c(cm(header_height), cm(header_space), share(.x), cm(row_gap))) %>%
    do.call(grid::unit.c, .)
  heights <- heights[-length(heights)] # no gap after the last row
  # Widths of the grid columns: plot, gap, plot, ... (no gap after the last column)
  widths  <- head(rep(c(1, column_gap), n_columns), -1)

  list(
    # headers first, then plots, matching the order of the areas in design
    plot   = wrap_plots(c(headers, cells$plot), design = design, widths = widths, heights = heights),
    # printed height in cm: the subfigures plus headers, spaces and gaps
    height = sum(row_heights + header_height + header_space) + (length(row_heights) - 1) * row_gap
  )
}

# Writes the PDF (16 cm wide, on a 2x canvas like all figures)
# set.seed(): the jittered points of Figure B.1 are drawn anew each time the plot is drawn
save_combined <- function(combined, file) {
  set.seed(2026)
  ggsave(file.path("output", "figures", paste0(file, ".pdf")), combined$plot,
         device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, width = figure_width, height = combined$height, units = "cm",
         scale = figure_scale)
}
```

# Combined Figures

```{r combine}
# For each figure (row of figures): build it and save the PDF to output/figures/
# pwalk() passes the columns to the function by name
figures %>%
  pwalk(function(file, layout, panels) {
    save_combined(combine_figure(layout, panels), file)
  })
```
